text: Grant access per engagement through membership, with a role assigned on each engagement. A person may hold different roles on different engagements.
Show users only the clients, engagements and projects they are members of, except roles granted portfolio-wide read access (engagement executive, PMO, finance, auditor).
Restrict cost rates, salary-derived costs, margins and internal commercial notes to finance, engagement executives and engagement managers unless explicitly granted.
Support restricted engagements whose existence and data are hidden from everyone except named members, including portfolio-wide roles.
Limit external client users to their own engagements and to records explicitly flagged as client-visible.
Support time-bound access (start and end dates) for contractors and auditors, removed automatically at expiry.
Record every grant, change and removal of access in the audit log.
Provide an access review report per engagement for periodic review by the engagement manager.
Separate administration rights from data access, so system administrators have no default access to engagement content.
Maintain client records: legal and trading name, ABN, client code, sector, government or private, addresses, billing entity, default payment terms, currency and status.
Maintain client contacts with title, role, contact details and relationship owner, reusable across stakeholder registers, approvals and distribution lists.
Support parent–child client hierarchies (for example a department and its agencies, or a group and its subsidiaries) for roll-up reporting.
Record master agreements and panel arrangements (head agreements, standing offers, deeds) with term, expiry, rate schedules and key terms, and alert before expiry (default 90 days).

Record client obligations that affect delivery: clearance and onboarding requirements, data classification, reporting frequency, template and recipients, and invoicing rules (such as PO number on invoice or an invoice portal).
Provide a client overview: current and past engagements, agreements, revenue to date, WIP, debtors, key contacts, open high risks and issues, and satisfaction scores.
Prevent duplicate client records by matching on ABN and name, and synchronise client and contact data with the CRM (INT-006).
Record client satisfaction survey results per engagement and show trends.

Create an engagement for a client with name, code, description, objectives, type (advisory, delivery, managed service, capacity), dates, engagement executive, engagement manager, client sponsor, status, data classification and security requirements.
Create an engagement from a won CRM opportunity, carrying over client, value, scope summary, proposed team and commercial model.
Allow an engagement to contain one or more projects: add projects at any time, move a project between engagements of the same client (audited), and close projects independently.

Record contractual instruments: master agreement reference, SOWs, work orders and variations, with value, term, commercial model, deliverables, payment terms, key personnel, liability caps and special conditions.
Record client POs with number, value, GST basis (inclusive or exclusive), validity dates and any financial-year limits, and track consumption (invoiced plus approved unbilled) against each PO.
Allocate funding from SOWs and POs to projects many-to-many, and prevent allocations exceeding an instrument's value.
Define engagement governance: steering committee membership, meeting cadence, decision rights, delegations and escalation path, reusable for project boards.
Record cross-project dependencies within the engagement, and with other engagements for the same client, and show their impact on dependent milestones.
Maintain engagement-level RAID registers; escalate a project item to the engagement level; link related items across projects.

Provide an engagement dashboard that rolls up all projects: health by dimension, milestones due in the next four weeks, top risks and issues, open changes, financials (budget, actuals, forecast, EAC, margin, PO burn) and resourcing.
Calculate engagement health from project health using a configurable rule (BR-16), with manual override requiring justification.
Record engagement objectives and map each project to the objectives it supports.
Track key contract dates (expiry, extension options, renewal decisions) and alert the engagement manager at 90, 60 and 30 days.
Record engagement reporting obligations (cadence, default report template, distribution list, required governance meetings) and show compliance with them.
Show an engagement roadmap with all projects, stages and key milestones on one timeline.
Support extension and renewal: create a new SOW or variation and carry forward open projects, RAID items and team.
Record growth opportunities identified during delivery and pass them to the CRM.
Create a project in an engagement from a project template that pre-populates its delivery profile, stages, standard tasks, standard risks, mandatory artefacts and gate criteria.

Capture a project brief or charter: background, objectives, scope in and out, deliverables, success criteria, constraints, assumptions, dependencies, approach, stakeholders, governance, indicative budget and timeline.
Record the Firm's commercial approval (price, cost, margin, risk, contract terms), routed by value and margin thresholds; for example, margin below target needs engagement executive approval.
Record or link the client's business case (options, benefits, costs, timescales, risks) and require continued business justification to be confirmed at each stage gate.

Record governance roles with named people from the Firm and the client, using configurable role sets (for example PRINCE2 executive, senior user, senior supplier, project assurance and change authority; or sponsor and steering committee).
Record a RACI matrix for key deliverables and activities.
Set project and stage tolerances for time, cost, scope, quality, benefits, risk and sustainability; tolerances drive automated monitoring and exception alerts (STS-008).
Define stage gates with criteria, required artefacts and approvers; record decisions (proceed, proceed with conditions, re-plan, stop) and track conditions to closure.
Block, or flag per configuration, progression to the next stage until mandatory gate artefacts are complete and approved.

Classify each project by size, complexity and risk (for example small, medium, large). The classification sets governance intensity: reporting frequency, gate requirements and whether earned value is mandatory.
Record how the delivery profile has been tailored for the project, and why.
Record the project's management approaches (risk, quality, change, communication, sustainability, data) as structured fields or linked documents.
Generate a project initiation document (PID) from captured data using the report engine (section 8).
Support PMO assurance health checks with a configurable checklist, findings and actions.
Maintain a work breakdown structure of stages, work packages and tasks, at least eight levels deep.
Support product-based planning: product breakdown structure and product descriptions (purpose, composition, quality criteria, quality method, owner, approver).

Schedule tasks with start and finish dates, duration, effort, percent complete, assigned resources, and dependencies (finish-to-start, start-to-start, finish-to-finish, start-to-finish) with leads and lags.
Calculate the critical path and total float, and highlight critical tasks.
Maintain milestones, including client-dependency and payment milestones, with planned, baseline, forecast and actual dates.
Store multiple baselines (original, plus approved re-baselines with reason and approval reference) and show variance against the current approved baseline.
Present Gantt and list views of the schedule.
Present Kanban board, calendar and timeline views.
Import and export schedules from and to Microsoft Project and Excel.
Support agile planning: product backlog (epics, features, user stories) with priority, estimates and acceptance criteria; sprints with goals, capacity and commitment; and release plans.
Calculate agile measures: velocity, sprint burn-down, release burn-up, cumulative flow and scope change.
Support hybrid plans where agile iterations sit inside predictive stages and roll progress up to stage milestones.
Let assignees update task status, percent complete or remaining effort, and comments, on web and mobile.
Flag schedule slippage: milestones forecast later than baseline, overdue tasks, and milestones put at risk by late predecessors or dependencies.
Provide reusable plan templates for common engagement types (for example discovery, business case, implementation, assurance review).
Provide a four-week look-ahead of tasks, milestones and deliverables for status reporting.
Model what-if re-plans without changing the live plan until approved.
Maintain a scope statement for each project and engagement, with in-scope and out-of-scope items linked to the SOW.
Maintain a deliverables register: ID, title, description, SOW reference, owner, planned, baseline, forecast and actual dates, status, version, acceptance criteria and client approver.

Support deliverable acceptance: submission to the client approver (in CEMS or the portal), review period per contract (default 10 business days), acceptance or rejection with comments, deemed acceptance where the contract allows, and stored evidence.
Link deliverables to billing milestones, so that acceptance marks the milestone ready to invoice.
Allow scope changes only through change control, and flag deliverables added or removed outside it.
Maintain an optional requirements register with traceability from business need to requirement, deliverable and acceptance test.

Maintain a resource pool of employees, contractors and subcontractors: role and grade, practice, location, employment type, standard hours, cost rate (restricted under ACC-003), skills and proficiency, certifications, security clearances with level and expiry, and availability.
Alert resource and engagement managers before clearances or certifications required by an engagement expire (default 60 days).
Let project managers raise resource requests (role, skills, clearance, hours or FTE, dates, location) and resource managers fulfil them with named people.
Record allocations as tentative or confirmed, by hours or percentage of full time per week, at project level and optionally at task level.
Show capacity against demand by person, role, practice and period, net of leave and public holidays by state and territory, highlighting over- and under-allocation.
Calculate planned and actual utilisation (billable and non-billable) by person, team and practice.
Search and match people to requests by skills, clearance, availability and cost.
Allow placeholder (unnamed) roles in plans and forecasts until named people are confirmed.
Record engagement onboarding requirements (inductions, building access, client system accounts, clearance sponsorship) and track completion for each team member.
Record key personnel named in the contract, and alert the engagement manager when a key person is removed, reallocated or goes on extended leave.
Show an engagement team view: who is on which project, in what role, at what allocation, with onboarding status.
Feed allocations into the labour forecast (FIN-019).
Let users record time daily or weekly against project tasks or project-level codes, with billable flag, work type and notes.
Provide non-project time codes: leave, training, business development, practice development and internal projects.
Enforce timesheet deadlines (default: Monday 10:00 am local time for the previous week) with reminders and escalation for late submission.
Route timesheets to the project manager for approval (engagement manager as alternate), support line-level approval and rejection, and lock approved time.
Validate entries: block time on closed projects and tasks; warn or block (configurable) time on unassigned tasks, above a daily maximum (default 12 hours), or beyond budget or PO limits.
Convert hours to billable days using the contract's day length (for example 7.5 or 8 hours) and rounding rule (BR-12).
Produce client timesheet extracts in the client's format, and capture client sign-off where the contract requires it.
Record expenses (travel, accommodation, meals, materials) with receipt image, GST amount, billable flag, contract mark-up rules and an approval workflow.
Import third-party and subcontractor costs and supplier invoices from the accounting system against projects and cost types.
Correct approved time only through a controlled adjustment with reason and audit trail; corrections to closed periods post to the current open period.
Suggest time entries from the user's Outlook calendar.

Maintain risk registers at project and engagement level: ID, title, cause–event–effect description, category, owner, actionee, date raised, proximity, likelihood, consequence, inherent and residual ratings, response strategy and actions, trend, status, linked items, client-visible flag and include-in-report flag.
Use a configurable likelihood × consequence matrix (default 5 × 5) with descriptors aligned to the Firm's risk framework, and allow a client-specific matrix per engagement.
Manage threats and opportunities with matching response types (threats: avoid, reduce, transfer, share, accept, prepare contingent plans; opportunities: exploit, enhance, share, reject).
Quantify risks where needed: cost and schedule impact ranges (minimum, most likely, maximum) and expected value.
Hold contingency and management reserve per project, and record drawdowns against risks or approved changes, with approval (FIN-011).
Prompt owners to review risks on a cycle set by rating (default weekly for high and extreme, fortnightly for others) and flag overdue reviews.
Escalate risks above a rating threshold, or forecast to breach tolerance, to the engagement level and notify the engagement manager (BR-15).
Provide inherent and residual heat maps, risk trends over time, and top-risk lists for dashboards and reports.
Keep a full history of rating, owner and status changes, to support trends and "changes since last report".
Provide a library of common consulting risks (for example subject-matter expert availability, scope creep, key person dependency, delayed system access) to seed registers.
Record the project's risk management approach: appetite, scales, roles and review frequency.
Run Monte Carlo cost and schedule risk analysis.

Maintain issue registers at project and engagement level: ID, title, description, type (problem or concern, request for change, off-specification, client escalation), priority, severity, owner, raised date, target resolution date, status, resolution, impacts and links.
Convert a request for change or off-specification into a change request, carrying over its data and keeping the link.
Escalate issues beyond tolerance or authority (configurable by severity) to the engagement manager or board, with an exception notification.

Maintain an assumptions log: assumption, source (such as the SOW), owner, validate-by date, status (open, validated, invalid) and impact if invalid. Invalidating an assumption prompts a linked risk, issue or change.

Maintain a dependencies register: direction (inbound or outbound), type (internal, client, third party, cross-project), provider, receiver, need-by date, status, linked milestones and impact. Overdue client dependencies are flagged prominently.
Maintain a decisions log: decision, context and options, decision-maker, date, forum, rationale, impacts and links.
Maintain an actions log: action, owner (Firm or client), due date, source (meeting, RAID item, gate condition) and status, with reminders when overdue.
Provide a combined RAID view with filtering, sorting, bulk update and export to Excel.
Flag RAID items as client-visible and include-in-report, with report inclusion defaulted by rule (open high and extreme risks, high-severity issues, overdue client dependencies, decisions required).
Show the age of RAID items and highlight items not reviewed within their cycle.
Raise RAID items from meeting minutes, a project email address, or Microsoft Teams.
Record change requests: ID, title, description, reason, requester (client or Firm), type (scope, schedule, cost, resource, contract), date raised, priority and status.
Capture impact on scope, schedule, cost and price, resources, quality, risk, benefits and contract terms; for priced changes, calculate cost, price and margin from estimates and rate cards.

Route change requests for approval by change authority thresholds (for example project manager up to a set value or number of days, engagement manager up to a higher value, steering committee or client above that), including client approval where required.
On approval, update the affected baselines (scope, schedule, budget, price) with a link to the change, keeping prior baselines.
Generate a change request or contract variation document from a template for signature, and record the executed variation (number, value, date).
Show the financial effect of pending changes separately in forecasts and scenarios (FIN-024).
Maintain a change log per project and engagement showing cumulative approved variations against the original contract value.
Flag time booked to work linked to unapproved changes as a commercial risk.
Track implementation of approved changes and close them when complete.
Record each project's quality management approach: standards, review methods, roles and acceptance responsibilities.
Record quality criteria and quality methods for each deliverable (its product description).
Maintain a quality register of planned and actual quality activities (peer review, QA review, testing, client walkthrough) with reviewers, dates, results and follow-up actions.
Require an internal quality review before a deliverable can be marked Submitted, configurable by deliverable class (for example engagement executive review of final reports).
Record review findings and defects against deliverables with severity and resolution.
Report quality measures: first-time acceptance rate, rework cycles, findings by severity and overdue reviews.
Record client feedback on individual deliverables.

Maintain an engagement stakeholder register shared by its projects: organisation, role, influence, interest, attitude, current and desired engagement level (unaware, resistant, neutral, supportive, leading), communication preferences and relationship owner.
Show stakeholders on a power–interest grid and an engagement assessment matrix (current against desired level).
Maintain a communication plan (audience, information needed, purpose, channel, frequency, owner, template) and track delivery against it.
Manage distribution lists per engagement and report type, for internal and client recipients.
Record governance meetings and workshops (agenda, attendees, minutes, decisions, actions), with decisions and actions flowing to their logs.
Generate steering committee packs and meeting agendas from templates using the report engine (section 8).
Record stakeholder interactions and relationship notes.
Schedule governance meetings through the Outlook calendar.
Require a status update for each active project per reporting period (default weekly; period and cut-off per BR-01), with reminders before the cut-off.

Capture in each status update: overall RAG and RAG for schedule, budget, scope, resources, risks and issues, and quality (dimensions configurable), each with commentary; executive summary; achievements this period; planned activities next period; decisions required; escalations; and client actions outstanding.

Pre-populate each update with system data: milestones achieved and missed, four-week look-ahead, RAID changes since the last update, change requests raised and approved, financial position, schedule and cost indices, and hours recorded.

Calculate a suggested RAG for each dimension from data and tolerances (BR-03), show it beside the manager's rating, and require justification when the chosen rating is better than the calculated one. This guards against "watermelon" reporting: green outside, red inside.
Roll the previous period's narrative forward as a starting point, marking fields carried over unchanged.
Route status updates to the engagement manager for review, who approves them or returns them with comments.
Keep the history of all status updates and show RAG trends (default last 12 periods).
Monitor tolerances continuously and raise exception alerts when a forecast breaches tolerance for time, cost, scope, quality, benefits, risk or sustainability.
Generate exception reports from a template, capturing cause, consequences, options, recommendation and lessons.
Show engagement managers and the PMO a submission tracker: which projects have submitted, are late, or await approval.
Lock status updates once used in an issued report; later edits create a new version with audit (BR-07).
Accept checkpoint reports from work package or team leads that feed the project status update.
Support status update entry on mobile devices.

Maintain a benefits register per engagement and project: benefit, description, type (financial or non-financial, cashable or non-cashable), client owner, measure, baseline, target, timing, enabling deliverables and status.
Record benefit measurements over time, including after project closure, against targets.
Record dis-benefits alongside benefits.
Produce a benefits review plan at closure, with review dates and owners.
Flag benefits and outcomes the client has approved for use as case studies or credentials.
Maintain a lessons log per project and engagement: what happened, impact, root cause, recommendation, category, tags, raised by and date.
Prompt lesson capture at stage gates and closure, and support agile retrospectives.
Publish selected lessons to a cross-engagement knowledge base, with client-confidential details removed or restricted.
Suggest relevant lessons when a project is created, matched by engagement type, client, sector and tags.
Track actions arising from lessons (such as updating a template or method) to closure.

Provide a configurable closure checklist: deliverables accepted, RAID items closed or transferred, final invoice issued, time and costs finalised, people released, client feedback obtained, lessons recorded, documents archived, access revoked.
Prevent closure until mandatory checklist items are complete or an exception is approved.
Generate an end project report (performance against baseline for scope, schedule, cost, quality and benefits; lessons; follow-on actions) from a template.
Transfer open risks, issues and actions to the engagement, another project or an operational owner on closure.
Close time codes automatically on project closure, after a grace period for final timesheets (default 10 business days).
Support premature closure (cancellation) with a reason, and calculate the final financial position.
Close an engagement only when all its projects are closed and contractual obligations (final invoice, handover, return or destruction of client data) are complete.
Set closed projects and engagements to read-only and retain them under the retention rules (DAT-001).
Maintain a document register per project and engagement: title, type, version, status, owner, classification and location.
Store documents in the Firm's repository (for example SharePoint) and link them to CEMS records without duplicating storage, respecting repository permissions.
Create a standard folder structure in the repository when an engagement or project is created.
Attach documents and evidence to any record (RAID item, change, deliverable, gate decision).
Retain version history for documents held or linked by CEMS.
Apply sensitivity labels (the Firm's labels, or Australian Government protective markings where required) and enforce their handling rules.
Search across records and attached documents within the user's permissions.

Provide a configurable workflow engine for approvals (status updates, timesheets, expenses, change requests, gate decisions, forecasts, report templates, reports) with sequential and parallel steps, delegation, and escalation on timeout.
Notify users of assignments, approvals, due and overdue items, and threshold breaches, in the app and by email.
Send notifications and approval actions to Microsoft Teams.
Let users choose immediate or daily-digest delivery for non-mandatory notifications.
Give each user a "My work" view: tasks, actions, approvals, owned RAID items, and timesheets and status updates due.
Support approval delegation during leave, with audit.
Support comments and @mentions on records.
Provide a portfolio dashboard across clients and engagements, filterable by client, engagement manager, practice, sector and status, showing health, financials, milestones, risks and utilisation.
Provide engagement and project dashboards (ENG-010).
Drill down from portfolio to client, engagement, project and individual records.
Provide exception lists: projects at risk, late status updates, PO burn alerts, contract and clearance expiries, overdue RAID reviews.
Provide a self-service report builder (fields, filters, grouping) with saved views and export to Excel, CSV and PDF.
Expose a governed analytics model (for example for Power BI) with row-level security matching CEMS permissions.
Show trends: RAG history, forecast movements, margin trend and RAID ageing.
Provide a secure portal for client stakeholders, using external identities with multi-factor authentication, scoped to their engagements.
Let client users view and download issued reports and deliverables, and view client-visible RAID items and actions.
Let client approvers accept or reject deliverables and approve change requests with comments, recorded as auditable approvals.
Let client users update the status of client-owned actions and dependencies.
Never expose internal-only data to client users (cost rates, costs, margins, internal notes, internal RAID items), enforced at the data layer and covered by automated tests.
Manage users, roles and engagement memberships, provisioned from Microsoft Entra ID groups (INT-001).

Configure delivery profiles (for example PRINCE2-aligned, PMBOK-aligned, agile, hybrid): lifecycle stages, gate criteria, mandatory artefacts and terminology (such as "stage" or "phase", "project board" or "steering committee").

Configure reference data: risk matrices and categories, RAG rules and thresholds, tolerance defaults, work and expense types, public holidays by state and territory, financial calendar and reporting periods.
Configure workflows and delegations of authority, including approval thresholds by value and margin.
Add custom fields to key records (client, engagement, project, RAID item, deliverable); custom fields become available as report tokens.
Configure numbering schemes, for example client code, engagement code and project number.
Maintain project, plan, RAID and closure templates.
Show system health, integration logs and scheduled jobs (such as scheduled report drafts).

Support these commercial models per project or SOW: time and materials (T&M); capped T&M (not to exceed); fixed price; milestone-based fixed price; retainer or managed service (recurring fee); and outcome-based fees. A project may have more than one billing arrangement, for example a fixed-price phase plus T&M support.
Build a price from effort estimates by role and rate, plus expenses, contingency and risk premium, showing the resulting price, cost, margin and effective day rate.
Maintain total contract value as original value plus approved variations, by SOW and by project.

Maintain charge-out rate cards at Firm, client, agreement or panel, and engagement level, by role or grade (optionally by named person), with effective dates, unit (hour or day) and currency. Resolve the applicable rate by precedence: named person, engagement, agreement or panel, client, Firm standard.
Maintain cost rates per person (fully loaded salary cost or contractor rate) with effective dates, visible only to authorised roles (ACC-003).
Apply rate changes, such as contracted annual indexation, from an effective date and show their effect on forecasts.
Apply discounts, rebates and volume tiers defined in agreements, at invoice or engagement level.

Create project budgets by stage or work package, cost type (labour, contractors, expenses, third-party products and services, contingency) and month, either top-down or bottom-up from the resource plan.
Hold the cost budget and revenue budget separately and calculate budgeted margin.
Baseline the budget on approval and keep every baseline; change it only through approved change requests or an approved re-baseline with a reason (BR-10).
Hold contingency (for identified risks) and management reserve outside the performance measurement baseline, and record drawdowns with approval and justification.
Roll budgets up to engagement, client and portfolio level.
Calculate labour actuals from approved timesheets: hours × cost rate for cost, and hours × applicable charge-out rate for revenue value (T&M) or standard value (fixed price).
Import non-labour actuals (expenses, supplier invoices) from the accounting system, mapped to projects and cost types.
Record commitments (subcontractor orders, confirmed allocations not yet worked) and show them alongside actuals.
Refresh actuals at least daily and on demand.
Reconcile project actuals to the general ledger at month-end and flag differences.
Produce a monthly, time-phased forecast of cost, revenue, billing and margin to completion for each project, combining actuals to date with the forecast for remaining periods.

Generate the labour forecast automatically from resource allocations (hours × cost rate and × charge-out rate), letting the project manager adjust hours, add placeholder roles and add non-labour forecasts.

Support alternative estimate-at-completion methods, recording the chosen method and justification: bottom-up from the resource plan; EAC = BAC ÷ CPI; EAC = AC + (BAC − EV); EAC = AC + (BAC − EV) ÷ (CPI × SPI); and manual override.
Calculate EAC, VAC, percentage of budget consumed, forecast margin and variance against baseline per project, and roll them up to the engagement.
Run a monthly forecast cycle with versioning, deadlines and approval (steps below).
Compare forecast versions (current, prior month, baseline) and require commentary on movements above a threshold (BR-14).
Model scenarios (for example base, best and worst case; with or without pending changes; with expected extensions) without changing the approved forecast.
Forecast portfolio revenue by month for the financial year, showing contracted work, signed but unstarted SOWs and probability-weighted CRM pipeline separately.
Track forecast accuracy: forecast against actual by month, by project and by engagement manager.
Forecast the date each PO or contract will be exhausted from forecast burn, and alert when it falls before the planned end date (BR-05).
Refresh the labour forecast weekly from approved time and current allocations, so weekly reports show a current EAC between monthly cycles.

Calculate earned value measures for projects whose classification requires them (GOV-010): planned value, earned value, actual cost, schedule and cost variance, SPI, CPI, TCPI and EAC, at project, stage and work package level.
Support earning methods per work package: 0/100, 50/50, weighted milestones, physical percent complete and apportioned effort.
Plot S-curves of planned value, earned value, actual cost and forecast, and trend CPI and SPI over time.
Calculate release-level earned value for agile projects from completed against planned story points.

Recognise revenue per period by commercial model, using rules agreed with Finance in line with AASB 15: T&M as time and expenses are delivered; fixed price over time using a configured measure of progress (cost-to-cost input method, or milestones as an output method); retainers evenly over the service period.

Generate a billing schedule per SOW or PO (T&M billing by period, for example monthly in arrears; milestone billing on acceptance; fixed-fee instalments; recurring fees), giving an invoice forecast by date.

Prepare draft invoices with supporting detail (timesheet extract by person and day, PO number, SOW reference, GST) for review by the engagement manager and finance, then send approved invoices to the accounting system for issue.
Synchronise invoice status (issued, paid, overdue, disputed) from the accounting system and calculate debtor days.
Calculate WIP and billed-in-advance balances per project, age WIP (0–30, 31–60, 61–90, over 90 days) and alert on aged WIP above a threshold.
Record WIP write-ups and write-downs with approval and reason codes, and report realisation.
Apply client billing rules: hourly or daily billing, day length and rounding (BR-12), billing caps, non-billable categories, expense mark-ups and travel rules.

Forecast monthly cash receipts from the invoice forecast and payment terms, and cash payments for subcontractor and third-party costs, giving a net cash flow forecast per engagement and for the portfolio.
Support a financial calendar (default Australian financial year, 1 July to 30 June) with monthly periods and period locking after month-end close; later transactions post to the open period.
Store amounts exclusive of GST, apply GST by tax code (default 10%), and compare PO consumption on the same GST basis as the PO (BR-13).
Support engagements in other currencies with exchange rates, reporting in AUD.
Enforce delegations of financial authority for budget changes, write-downs, discounts and forecast approval.
Keep a full audit trail of financial changes: who, what, when, and before and after values.
Support multiple legal entities and inter-entity resource charging.

Provide standard financial reports: project financial summary; engagement profit and loss; budget, actual and forecast by month; EAC trend; margin by project, engagement, client and practice; PO and contract burn with remaining funds; WIP and debtor ageing; revenue forecast by month for the financial year; utilisation and realisation; forecast movements; and the financial impact of changes.
Visualise budget and PO burn-down, revenue burn-up against contract value, S-curves, margin trend and monthly revenue.
Expose financial figures as report tokens (Appendix A), with audience controls so client-audience reports never show cost or margin (RPT-021).
Export financial data to Excel and to the analytics model (DSH-006).

Maintain a report template library with metadata: name, description, report type (weekly status, steering committee, monthly financial, exception, end stage, end project, PID, change request), scope (Firm-wide, client or engagement), level (project, engagement or portfolio), audience (internal or client), output formats, owner, version and status (draft, published, retired).
Let authorised users (the PMO for the library; engagement managers for their own engagements) upload templates as Microsoft Word (.docx) files.
Accept PowerPoint (.pptx) and Excel (.xlsx) templates.
Reject macro-enabled files (.docm, .pptm, .xlsm) and files over the size limit (default 20 MB); validate file type by content, not extension; and scan uploads for malware.
Preview a template filled with sample data, or with a selected live project the user can access, before publishing.
Version templates: a new upload creates a new version, earlier versions are kept, issued reports stay linked to the version used, and retired templates remain in history.
Require PMO approval before a template is published (configurable).
Assign default templates per engagement and report type, and allow another permitted template to be chosen at generation.

Provide starter templates in Word and PowerPoint for weekly project and weekly engagement reports, plus a downloadable token reference with descriptions, data types, formats and examples (Appendix A).
Preserve the template's branding and styles (logos, colours, fonts, headers and footers), and insert dynamic images such as the client logo from the client record.
Clone a template to adapt it for another client or engagement.
Replace single-value tokens, with formatting helpers for dates, numbers, AUD currency, percentages and text case.

Repeat table rows and sections over collections (projects, milestones, deliverables, risks, issues, actions, decisions, dependencies, changes, people, financial lines), with filtering, sorting and row limits such as "top five risks".
Show or hide content conditionally on data, for example an exception section only when a tolerance is breached.
Render RAG indicators as coloured cells, shapes or icons that always carry a text label, so colour is never the only signal (WCAG 2.2).
Render standard charts into templates as images: budget burn-down, milestone timeline, RAG trend and risk heat map.
Bind data to native PowerPoint and Excel charts.
Render rich-text narrative (bold, italics, bullets, numbered lists, links) using the template's own styles.
Support engagement-level templates that loop over each in-scope project and add engagement sections: summary, consolidated financials, engagement RAID and cross-project dependencies.
Make custom fields (ADM-005) available as tokens automatically.

Classify every token as client-safe or internal-only, and block internal-only tokens (cost, margin, cost rates, internal notes, internal RAID) from client-audience templates at validation and at generation.
Keep the template language logic-limited: no arbitrary code execution, and no access to data outside the token catalogue and the user's permissions (NFR-008).
Provide "changes since last report" tokens: RAG movements (up, down, steady), new and closed RAID items, milestone date movements, and forecast movement since the previous issued report.
Parse each uploaded template and list every token found, with its location (page, slide or cell).

Validate tokens against the catalogue and report errors with locations: unknown tokens, malformed syntax, unclosed loops or conditions, and internal-only tokens in client templates. Templates with errors cannot be published.

Support client-supplied templates without CEMS tokens: detect Word content controls (by tag or title), bookmarks and marked placeholder text, and let the user map each one to a token or narrative field on a mapping screen. The mapping is saved with the template version.
Flag template fields with no matching data, and offer to create a custom field (ADM-005) or a narrative field for them.

Let the engagement manager generate a report by selecting: engagement; scope (one project, selected projects, or all projects in the engagement); report type; template (from those permitted); reporting period (default the current week); audience; and output formats.

Run a readiness check before generation and show the results: status updates submitted and approved for each in-scope project, timesheets outstanding, overdue RAID reviews, milestones without current forecasts, and empty narrative fields the template requires. The user can return to fix gaps, or proceed with the warnings recorded against the report.
Freeze an immutable snapshot of all data used in the report at generation, with an as-at timestamp, so the report can be reproduced exactly and later data changes never alter it.

Provide an in-app editing step for report-level narrative (for example engagement summary and key messages) before final rendering. Project data changes only if the user chooses to save an edit back to the status update.
Render reports as Word (.docx) and PDF, preserving template formatting, with PDFs tagged for accessibility.
Render reports as PowerPoint (.pptx) and Excel (.xlsx).
Produce a draft for an engagement of up to 10 projects within 60 seconds (95th percentile); run larger reports in the background and notify the user when ready.
Name files by a configurable convention, for example {ClientCode}_{EngagementCode}_WeeklyReport_{WeekEnding}_v{n}.
Allow drafts to be regenerated any number of times before issue, keeping every version with its author and time.
Schedule automatic draft generation (for example Friday 9:00 am) for engagements with a default template, and notify the engagement manager when the draft is ready.
Generate the client and internal versions of a report from the same snapshot in one action.
Batch-generate one report type across several engagements, for example the PMO's internal portfolio pack.
Manage report status (Draft, In review, Approved, Issued, plus Superseded and Withdrawn) with configurable approvers, for example the engagement executive for client reports.
On issue, lock the report and its snapshot and mark the underlying status updates as reported. A correction is issued as a new version that supersedes the earlier one, with a recorded reason.
Apply sensitivity labels and protective markings to generated files (header, footer and document metadata) based on the engagement's classification.
Email issued reports through Microsoft 365 to the engagement's distribution list, as an attachment, a secure link or both, using a configurable message template.
Publish issued reports to the client portal (CPT-002).
Record each distribution (recipients, date and time, channel) in the engagement's communications log.
Allow external distribution only to recipients on the engagement's distribution list, unless an authorised user approves an exception.
Keep a searchable archive of all reports per engagement and project, filterable by period, type and status.
Compare two report periods side by side.
Offer AI-drafted text for narrative sections (executive summary, achievements, engagement summary across projects) using only data in the report snapshot.
Label AI drafts clearly, require a person to review and accept or edit them before inclusion, and record that AI assistance was used.
Use only an AI service approved by the Firm, with data processed in Australia where required, no use of Firm or client data for model training, and the same access controls as the requesting user.
Allow AI assistance to be switched on or off per engagement, defaulting to off for restricted engagements and wherever the client has not agreed to its use.
Suggest RAID items from meeting notes or status narrative, for a person to confirm.

Retain engagement, project and financial records for at least seven years after engagement closure, consistent with the seven-year retention of financial records under the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth), with configurable retention by record type and legal hold.
De-identify or delete personal information that is no longer needed, subject to retention obligations (APP 11.2).
Keep archived data searchable and read-only.
Record client contractual data obligations (for example return or destruction of client data at contract end) and track them to completion.

Import active clients, engagements, projects, RAID logs, people, rate cards and open financial positions from spreadsheets and existing tools, using import templates with validation and error reports.
Import historical actuals (at least the current and prior financial year) for trend reporting.
Produce reconciliation reports comparing migrated data with source totals.
Apply mandatory fields and validation rules per entity and lifecycle state.
Provide a data quality dashboard for the PMO: records missing owners, overdue reviews, stale forecasts and projects without baselines.
Microsoft Entra ID — Single sign-on (SAML or OpenID Connect), MFA, group-based provisioning (SCIM) (Inbound)
Microsoft 365 email (Exchange Online) — Notifications and report distribution from a service mailbox (Outbound)
SharePoint and OneDrive — Document storage, folder provisioning, archive copy of issued reports (Both)
Microsoft Teams — Notifications, approvals and report links in engagement channels (Outbound)
Accounting system (to be confirmed, for example Xero, MYOB or Dynamics 365 Business Central) — Clients and debtors, invoices, payments, supplier costs, general ledger actuals (Both)
CRM (to be confirmed) — Won opportunities, clients, contacts and weighted pipeline in; engagement status and growth opportunities out (Both)
HR and payroll system — People, employment details, cost rate inputs, leave (Inbound)
Delivery tools (for example Jira, Azure DevOps) — Epics, stories, sprints and progress for agile projects (Inbound, optional outbound)
Microsoft Project and Excel — Schedule import and export (Both)
Power BI or data warehouse — Governed analytics model (Outbound)
E-signature service — Signature of change requests and variations (Both)
Approved AI service — Narrative drafting and suggestions (section 8.10) (Outbound)
Provide a documented REST API (OpenAPI) for core entities, secured with OAuth 2.0, and webhooks for key events (status update submitted, report issued, change approved, threshold breached).
Monitor integrations, retry failed messages, queue errors for resolution and alert administrators; processing is idempotent.

Define the system of record for each data object: CRM for prospects and pipeline; accounting for invoices, payments and the ledger; HR for employees; CEMS for engagements, projects, RAID, forecasts and reports.
Authenticate internal users through single sign-on with enforced MFA (phishing-resistant methods preferred), and external users through federated or guest identities with MFA.
Enforce role-based, engagement-scoped access with field-level restrictions (section 5.2) at the service and data layers, not only in the user interface.
Encrypt data in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (AES-256), with keys in a managed key service.

Align controls with ISO/IEC 27001 and the Firm's ISMS. For engagements handling Australian Government information, meet the client's required controls, such as the ISM, Essential Eight maturity targets and IRAP-assessed hosting for OFFICIAL: Sensitive information.
Complete independent penetration testing before go-live, annually and after major releases, and resolve critical and high findings before go-live.
Follow a secure development lifecycle that addresses the OWASP Top 10, with static code analysis and dependency scanning in the build pipeline.
Send security events (sign-ins, failed sign-ins, permission changes, exports, report distribution) to the Firm's security monitoring platform.

Treat uploaded templates and attachments as untrusted: scan for malware, strip active content, and render templates in an isolated service with a logic-limited template language that cannot execute code.
End inactive sessions after 30 minutes (configurable).
Log all data exports and restrict bulk export to authorised roles.
Handle personal information in line with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and the APPs, and complete a privacy impact assessment before go-live.
Collect only the personal information needed, and support access and correction requests.
Provide the logs and records needed to assess a suspected eligible data breach under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme.
Host production, backups and disaster recovery in Australian data centres, with no offshore access to data without the Firm's approval.
Achieve at least 99.5% availability per month during business hours (7:00 am to 7:00 pm Australian Eastern Time, Monday to Friday), excluding scheduled maintenance outside those hours.
Meet a recovery point objective of 1 hour or less and a recovery time objective of 4 hours or less.
Take daily backups (retained 35 days) and monthly backups (retained 12 months), and test restores at least quarterly.
Respond to 95% of screen interactions within 2 seconds under normal load.

Support at least 300 named users, 100 concurrent users, 50 active engagements, 300 active projects and 10 years of data without degradation. This sizing is indicative and will be confirmed in discovery.
Refresh dashboards within 5 seconds, and meet the report generation time in RPT-034.
Conform to WCAG 2.2 Level AA, for the application and for generated PDF reports.
Work on desktop, tablet and mobile; on mobile, support time entry, approvals, status updates and RAID entry.
Let a project manager complete a weekly status update without training, using in-app guidance, verified through usability testing.
Provide contextual help and role-based onboarding guides.
Keep an immutable audit trail of every create, update and delete on business records (user, timestamp, before and after values), retained per DAT-001.
Provide audit reports filterable by user, record and date range.
Use Australian English, AUD formatting, dd/mm/yyyy dates and the Australian financial year; store times in UTC and display them in the user's local time zone, including daylight saving.
Provide separate development, test, UAT and production environments, and mask production data before any use in lower environments.
Deploy through automated pipelines with automated tests; minor releases deploy without downtime.
Make workflows, templates, thresholds and delivery profiles configurable without a code release.
Provide monitoring, alerting and logging, with a defined support model and service levels.
Provide user guides, an administrator guide, API documentation, the data dictionary and a template author guide.
Maintain a software bill of materials, and use third-party components under licences compatible with the Firm's ownership of the solution.
Pilot with two engagements of different shapes (for example a multi-project T&M engagement and a fixed-price engagement) before wider rollout.
Run weekly reporting in parallel (current method and CEMS) for at least two cycles per pilot engagement, reconciling the outputs.
Migrate data under DAT-005 to DAT-007, with reconciliation signed off by finance and the engagement managers.
Deliver role-based training for engagement managers, project managers, team members, finance, the PMO and administrators, plus a template author guide.
Provide hypercare support for four weeks after each go-live.
Track adoption (status update timeliness, reports generated, forecast submission rates) for three months after go-live.
